questions.stem: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The ovum is released into the funnel of the oviduct and meets the sperm in its upper portion, so fusion occurs there. The zygote then divides as it travels down the oviduct and implants in the uterus about a week later.

distractorRationale.a: The ovary releases the ovum but sperm do not enter it
distractorRationale.c: The uterus is where the embryo implants and develops, after fertilisation
distractorRationale.d: The vagina receives the semen; the sperm must still swim to the oviduct

questions.stem: The testes are located in the scrotum outside the body cavity because sperm production requires

options.text: a temperature slightly lower than the core body temperature
a higher temperature than the rest of the body

questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis is most efficient a couple of degrees below 37 °C, and the scrotum, being outside the abdomen, provides that cooler environment. This is why a persistent high fever or tight clothing can temporarily reduce sperm production.

distractorRationale.b: The testes are enclosed in skin and never in contact with air
distractorRationale.c: Immune protection is not the reason for their external position
distractorRationale.d: A higher temperature reduces rather than increases sperm production

questions.stem: In a regular 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation usually occurs on about day
questions.explanation: Rising oestrogen from the developing follicle triggers a surge of LH around the midpoint of the cycle, and the follicle then ruptures to release the ovum. Day 1 is the first day of menstruation, so ovulation falls roughly two weeks later.

distractorRationale.a: Day 1 marks the beginning of menstruation, when the endometrium is shed
distractorRationale.b: By day 7 the follicle is still developing under the influence of FSH
distractorRationale.d: By day 28 progesterone is falling and the next menstruation is about to begin

questions.stem: Which hormone maintains the thickened lining of the uterus during the second half of the menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: After ovulation the empty follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone. Progesterone keeps the endometrium thick and well supplied with blood for a possible implantation, and it also inhibits FSH so that no new follicle develops.

distractorRationale.a: FSH stimulates follicle development in the first half of the cycle
distractorRationale.b: LH triggers ovulation itself, in a short surge around day 14
distractorRationale.d: Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone

questions.stem: Which substance passes from the blood of the foetus to the blood of the mother across the placenta?
questions.explanation: The foetus produces urea from protein metabolism but has no functioning excretory route of its own, so urea diffuses into the mother's blood for her kidneys to remove. Carbon dioxide travels the same way, while oxygen and nutrients travel in the opposite direction.

distractorRationale.a: Oxygen passes from mother to foetus, since the foetus cannot breathe
distractorRationale.b: Glucose is supplied by the mother for the foetus's respiration and growth
distractorRationale.d: Amino acids pass from mother to foetus for building new tissue

questions.stem: A sperm cell contains a middle piece packed with mitochondria. This is because the sperm needs

options.text: to store food for the developing embryo
a large supply of energy for the movement of its tail
enzymes to digest the egg membrane

questions.explanation: A sperm must swim a relatively enormous distance from the vagina to the upper oviduct, and lashing its tail consumes a great deal of ATP. The mitochondria in the middle piece carry out the aerobic respiration that supplies it, using fructose from the seminal fluid.

distractorRationale.a: Food reserves for the early embryo are stored in the cytoplasm of the ovum
distractorRationale.c: The digesting enzymes are in the acrosome, at the head of the sperm
distractorRationale.d: A sperm is haploid and carries only 23 chromosomes

questions.stem: The function of the amniotic fluid surrounding a developing foetus is to

options.text: protect the foetus from mechanical shock and allow it to move freely
remove urea from the foetal blood

questions.explanation: The fluid is contained in the amnion and acts as a shock absorber, spreading any pressure evenly so that a knock to the mother's abdomen does not injure the foetus. It also keeps the foetus at a steady temperature and lets its limbs move, which helps muscle development.

distractorRationale.a: Oxygen reaches the foetus through the placenta and umbilical cord
distractorRationale.c: Urea is removed across the placenta into the mother's blood
distractorRationale.d: The placenta, not the amniotic fluid, secretes pregnancy hormones

questions.stem: The blood of the mother and the blood of the foetus mix freely in the placenta.
questions.explanation: False. The two circulations are brought extremely close together but remain separate, and materials cross between them by diffusion and active transport. Separation matters because the mother's blood pressure would damage the delicate foetal vessels and their blood groups may be incompatible.

questions.stem: Menstruation does not occur if the ovum is fertilised. The reason is that

options.text: the ovary stops producing ova permanently
the corpus luteum persists and continues to secrete progesterone, so the endometrium is maintained
the uterus becomes too small to shed its lining
FSH levels rise sharply after fertilisation

questions.explanation: Menstruation happens when progesterone falls and the endometrium can no longer be maintained. A developing embryo signals the corpus luteum to survive rather than degenerate, so progesterone stays high, the lining is retained for implantation, and no period occurs — which is why a missed period is an early sign of pregnancy.

distractorRationale.a: Ovulation is suspended during pregnancy but the ovary is not permanently shut down
distractorRationale.c: The uterus enlarges greatly during pregnancy rather than shrinking
distractorRationale.d: FSH is inhibited by high progesterone, so no new follicle develops

questions.stem: State four functions of the placenta and explain three ways in which a sperm cell differs structurally from an ovum, relating each difference to its function.
markingGuide: Placenta function 1: allows oxygen to diffuse from the mother's blood to the foetal blood (1 mark)
Placenta function 2: allows glucose, amino acids, mineral salts, vitamins, water and antibodies to pass to the foetus (2 marks)
Placenta function 3: allows carbon dioxide and urea to pass from the foetus to the mother for excretion (2 marks)

Placenta function 4: secretes hormones, particularly progesterone and oestrogen, which maintain the pregnancy; accept also that it acts as a partial barrier keeping the two bloodstreams separate (1 mark)
Difference 1: the sperm is much smaller and has a tail, so it can swim to the ovum, whereas the ovum is non-motile (2 marks)
Difference 2: the sperm has a middle piece full of mitochondria to supply energy for swimming, which the ovum does not need (2 marks)

Difference 3: the ovum has abundant cytoplasm containing food reserves for the early embryo, while the sperm has almost none; accept also the acrosome of the sperm, which contains enzymes to penetrate the egg membrane (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The placenta should be described as a two-way exchange surface plus an endocrine organ, with the direction of travel stated for each substance. The gamete differences all follow from a division of labour: the sperm is stripped down for mobility and penetration, while the ovum is provisioned to support the embryo before implantation.

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for initiating the menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is crucial for the development of ovarian follicles and the initiation of the menstrual cycle. It stimulates the ovaries to produce estrogen, which regulates the cycle.

distractorRationale.a: Estrogen plays a role in regulating the menstrual cycle but is not the hormone that initiates it.
distractorRationale.b: Progesterone is involved in the latter part of the menstrual cycle and pregnancy, but it does not initiate the cycle.
distractorRationale.d: Luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers ovulation but does not initiate the menstrual cycle.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the vas deferens in the male reproductive system?
questions.explanation: The vas deferens is responsible for the transport of sperm from the epididymis to the ejaculatory duct during ejaculation. This function is critical for male fertility.

distractorRationale.a: Sperm production occurs in the testes, not the vas deferens.
distractorRationale.c: Testosterone is secreted by the Leydig cells in the testes, not by the vas deferens.
distractorRationale.d: Sperm is stored in the epididymis, not the vas deferens.

questions.stem: During which phase of the menstrual cycle does the endometrium thicken in preparation for a possible pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The luteal phase is characterized by the secretion of progesterone, which causes the endometrium to thicken in preparation for the implantation of a fertilized egg. If implantation does not occur, the cycle will restart.

distractorRationale.a: The menstrual phase involves shedding of the uterine lining, not thickening.
distractorRationale.b: The follicular phase focuses on follicle development and does not primarily involve endometrial thickening.
distractorRationale.c: The ovulatory phase is when ovulation occurs, but the thickening of the endometrium is mainly influenced by the luteal phase.

questions.stem: What role does the placenta play during pregnancy?

options.text: It provides nutrients and oxygen to the fetus
It is the site of fertilization

questions.explanation: The placenta serves as the interface between the mother and fetus, providing essential nutrients and oxygen while also removing waste products from fetal blood. It plays a vital role in fetal development.

distractorRationale.a: While the placenta does produce hormones, its primary function is nutrient and gas exchange.
distractorRationale.c: Fertilization occurs in the fallopian tubes, not in the placenta.
distractorRationale.d: The placenta does not store the embryo; it supports its development.

questions.stem: Which hormone is responsible for the release of the ovum from the ovary?
questions.explanation: Luteinizing hormone (LH) is responsible for triggering ovulation, which is the release of the ovum from the ovarian follicle. This is a crucial step in the menstrual cycle.

distractorRationale.a: Estrogen helps regulate the cycle but does not trigger ovulation.
distractorRationale.b: FSH promotes follicle development but is not the hormone that causes ovulation.
distractorRationale.d: Progesterone is involved after ovulation, particularly in maintaining the uterine lining.

questions.explanation: The average menstrual cycle lasts about 28 days, although it can vary from person to person. This cycle includes various phases that prepare the body for potential pregnancy.

distractorRationale.c: A 30-day cycle is longer than average but still within the normal range for some individuals.
distractorRationale.d: A 35-day cycle is considered longer than average and may also indicate irregularities.

distractorRationale.b: The seminal vesicle contributes fluid to semen but does not produce sperm.
distractorRationale.d: The prostate gland produces seminal fluid but is not involved in sperm production.

distractorRationale.c: Maintaining pregnancy is associated with the luteal phase, not the follicular phase.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the corpus luteum after ovulation?

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes fertilization?

options.text: The union of two sperm cells
The fusion of an ovum and a sperm cell
The implantation of a fertilized egg

questions.explanation: Fertilization is defined as the fusion of an ovum (egg) and a sperm cell, resulting in the formation of a zygote. This is the first step in the development of a new organism.

distractorRationale.a: Fertilization involves the union of an ovum and a sperm, not two sperm cells.
distractorRationale.c: Implantation occurs after fertilization when the zygote attaches to the uterine lining.
distractorRationale.d: Embryonic development occurs after fertilization and implantation.

questions.stem: Which part of the female reproductive system is responsible for the production of ova?

distractorRationale.c: The fallopian tube is the passageway through which ova travel to the uterus but does not produce them.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of luteinizing hormone (LH) in the menstrual cycle?

options.text: Stimulates the thickening of the uterine lining

questions.explanation: Luteinizing hormone (LH) plays a crucial role in the menstrual cycle by triggering ovulation, which is the release of an ovum from the ovary. This process is essential for fertilization to occur.

distractorRationale.a: While LH is involved in the menstrual cycle, it does not directly stimulate the thickening of the uterine lining; that is primarily influenced by progesterone.
distractorRationale.c: LH actually promotes follicle development prior to ovulation, rather than inhibiting it.
